timestamp_derivation: After the last content commit of this delivery and after every live proof it records: the appliance was restored twice from real backups, a third restore was deliberately made to fail, and the five journeys were walked on the deployed bundle at 172.21.60.25 on a desktop and an iPhone profile. Before the author timestamp of the commit that introduces this receipt.
what_was_authorised: One consolidated Hotel Admin usability mission covering five operator journeys, authorised end to end including implementation, targeted and regression tests, PRE-LIVE deployment, live verification, the required gates, a protected merge and governance synchronisation. The Product Owner declined a split and declined any depth trade-off: 'I did not authorize any depth trade-off or a split of the five requested journeys.'

the_five_journeys.1_appliance_and_licence: Activation and License were two destinations answering one question. They are now one page, /appliance, with one nav entry, one dashboard card and one licence-upload workflow. /license and /setup/enrollment redirect to it so a bookmarked operator lands where they meant to; both were verified live on desktop and on a phone.
the_five_journeys.2_activity: The audit log was a table of timestamps, actor uuids and dotted action codes. It is now an Activity screen: every one of the 40 live action codes has operator wording, a category and a severity; there is search, a period selector, category and security filters, and every row opens to the exact action, ids, IP and payload. The append-only model is untouched -- nothing was deleted, rewritten, fabricated or backfilled. 395 entries on the appliance render in plain English.
the_five_journeys.3_backups_and_restore: Rebuilt around Backup -> Verify -> Download -> Restore, with retention, schedule, disk and the nightly sweep kept in full in one disclosure below the journey rather than competing with it. Restore is the controlled live operation this mission authorised; it is described in detail below.
the_five_journeys.4_guest_activity: The inspection tab listed quote, revision and purchase uuids. It now reads, for each offer, the room it was offered to with its PMS interface, the package by name, whether it was taken and when, the price, and what access it granted -- in that order, in a sentence. Sixteen live offers on the appliance, and no uuid on the screen. No guest identifier is reproduced here: this record describes the shape of the screen, not the roster behind it.
the_five_journeys.5_usage_explorer: A new screen for the argument a guest starts about their data: by room or stay, and by device. Every total is the sum of durable accounting records and every session opens to the samples behind it -- nothing is estimated, interpolated or invented. Room travels only with its PMS Interface and Stay, and the device tab says in as many words that a MAC identifies equipment and not a person.

controlled_restore.authorisation: Explicitly authorised by the Product Owner as part of this mission, including live proof on PRE-LIVE and a deliberate failure and rollback proof.
controlled_restore.design: Capture the appliance's privilege state, take a safety dump, stop serving, load into a STAGING database, rename the live one aside, rename staging in, reinstate the privileges, verify integrity, restart the dependents. The destructive step is a rename, so rollback is a rename back and does not depend on a second dump being good. Nothing in the path retries a destructive step.
gates_before_it_will_start: the operator's password (step-up), checked by edged
the backup's own name typed out, checked by edged
a verification that still describes the bytes on disk, checked by scd as well as reported by edged
no maintenance already in progress, and an in-process single-flight guard
controlled_restore.live_proof_success: PRE-LIVE 172.21.60.25, 2026-09-20T09:26:39Z to 09:27:03Z, 24 seconds. Eight steps, all ok: 1491 ownership and access rules captured; safety dump db-safety-20260920T092639Z.sql.gz; maintenance on; load into staging (141 tables); swap; all 1491 rules reinstated and verified identical; integrity -- 141 tables and every table the appliance needs; serving again. THE DATA PROOF: 422 audit rows before, 415 after -- the rows written after the backup was taken are gone, which is what a restore means. The previous database is kept as stayconnect_site_before_20260920t092639z.
controlled_restore.live_proof_failure_and_rollback: A verified backup was corrupted in place -- same size, same nanosecond mtime -- so that it remained genuinely eligible and would fail at the load rather than at the gate. 09:35:24Z to 09:35:38Z: privileges captured, safety dump taken, maintenance on, load refused with 'missing data for column sequence_version'. Then: stayconnect_site oid 82681 before and 82681 after -- the SAME DATABASE, never opened; no set-aside database created; no staging left behind; maintenance cleared; all six services active; the guest portal answering 200. The operator is told which step failed and why.
controlled_restore.an_earlier_refusal_that_is_also_evidence: A first attempt at the failure proof re-pointed the verification marker at truncated bytes and was refused before the restore began: 'this backup has changed since it was verified; verify it again'. That is the eligibility gate working, and it left the previous outcome record untouched -- a precondition refusal is not a restore.

defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.what: A restore left the appliance unable to serve.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.detail: Backups are taken with pg_dump --no-owner --no-privileges. Fine while a dump was only ever loaded into a scratch database to be verified; not fine loaded into the database a hotel runs on. The restored database came up owned by the superuser with PUBLIC holding the default EXECUTE on every function. scd could not read pms_providers and exited; edged could not reach schema iam_v2 and exited; with schema access back edged still refused to serve, correctly, because PUBLIC held EXECUTE on iam_v2.apply_entitlement_transition; pmsd crash-looped until systemd gave up. Every service was behaving properly. The integrity check passed it because 141 tables were present and it had never been asked whether anyone could read them.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.fix: The privilege state now travels across the swap: captured from the live database before anything is touched, replayed after the rename, captured again and compared. Identical or roll back. Captured rather than written down, so the numbered migrations stay the single source of truth. The revokes are included -- an absent privilege is as deliberate as a present one.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.note: PRE-LIVE was repaired by this mechanism before it was code.

defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.what: A successful restore was reported to the operator as a failure.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.detail: edged's socket call gave up after fifteen seconds; scd finished successfully ten seconds later. Someone reading 'failed' about a destructive operation that is still running is one keystroke from starting a second one.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.fix: scd answers 202 and does the work in the background under its own context. The durable record gains `running` and is stamped in progress the moment a restore starts. The dialog polls it and treats a failed poll as what it is -- edged restarting, which the restore itself causes. The record is written by rename so a poller never reads half a document.

defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.what: The staging database could not be found immediately after being created.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.detail: CREATE DATABASE restore_20260920T090146Z created restore_20260920t090146z -- SQL folds unquoted identifiers -- and psql -d restore_20260920T090146Z was told no such database existed, because libpq passes a dbname through verbatim. It failed safely: the live database was never opened.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.fix: The stamp is lowercased where it becomes an identifier. A test pins it.

defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.what: Verify succeeded and the screen still showed the backup as unverified.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.detail: scd writes the marker as root; edged reads as `stayconnect`. The archives are handed to the service group at 0640; the marker was left root:root. A fact nobody could read.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.fix: The marker takes the same handover as the archive it vouches for.

defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.what: Guest Activity returned 500 on the appliance.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.detail: permission denied for table iam_v2.auth_contexts; svc_edged does not hold SELECT on it.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.fix: The query reads what edged is allowed to read. A taken offer is complete -- the purchase carries the stay, the earliest session on the entitlement carries the sign-in method. An UNTAKEN offer cannot show the room, because auth_contexts is the only link from a quote to a stay before the offer is taken; that column is left empty rather than inferred. All sixteen offers on this appliance were taken, so nothing is missing from real data today.

defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.what: Each restore left another full copy of the site behind, and nothing ever swept them.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.detail: Keeping the replaced database is how a restore is undone, but nothing removed the previous one. Separately, /opt/stayconnect/backups/db was never in the retention sweep at all -- Central retained its dumps, the appliance's own accumulated forever -- and Restore writes a 27MB safety copy per attempt into it, under a page that displays a disk gauge.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.fix: Exactly one database is kept aside, dropped only after the integrity and privilege checks pass. The appliance's database backups joined the existing sweep under the same rules: newest never deleted, pinned never deleted, KEEP_DB retained. The dry run on PRE-LIVE plans exactly the two September 17th dumps older than the newest seven.

defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.what: The Activity trail named half its actors with a uuid.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.detail: Rows with an actor id printed it raw; rows without said 'An operator'.
defects_found_by_running_it_on_the_appli.fix: The summary line resolves the operator directory to a name; the exact id stays in the record.

migration_0082.what_it_does: GRANT SELECT ON iam_v2.accounting_records AND iam_v2.devices TO svc_edged, so the Usage Explorer can read the usage it reports. No DDL, no DML, no writes, is_grantable = NO.
migration_0082.the_history_as_it_happened_and_it_is_not: It was APPLIED TO PRE-LIVE BEFORE Product-Owner approval. The Product Owner stopped the mission for it: 'The only genuine controlled-boundary issue you should have stopped for is migration 0082, because it changes database/service privileges and was applied to PRE-LIVE without prior Product Owner approval.' The exact scope was then presented, reviewed, and approved as applied. That sequence is recorded here deliberately and is not to be rewritten.
migration_0082.standing_instruction: No further controlled migration or privilege change without its own approval. That instruction was honoured: the auth_contexts grant Guest Activity would have benefited from was NOT applied, and the feature was built without it.

product_owner_decision_requested.id: one open decision, outside this mission
product_owner_decision_requested.what: GRANT SELECT ON iam_v2.auth_contexts TO svc_edged, as a numbered migration, so Guest Activity can attribute an offer that nobody took to the room it was offered to.
product_owner_decision_requested.why_it_is_not_in_this_delivery: It is a controlled privilege change and this mission does not carry that authorisation. It was not applied anywhere, and no migration file was created.
product_owner_decision_requested.what_it_costs_to_leave_it: Untaken offers show what was offered, when, at what price and that nobody took it, but not to whom. There are none on PRE-LIVE today.

verification.unit_and_regression: Go: gofmt, build, vet (including tags), production-tag build, test -count=1, all clean. Hotel Admin: 30 test files, 339 tests, all passing; tsc clean; production build clean.
verification.live_five_journeys: The deployed bundle at 172.21.60.25 driven in a real browser at 1440x900 and on an iPhone 13 profile: 14/14 checks, zero failing operator-API calls, zero horizontal overflow, screenshots kept.
verification.live_restore: One successful restore, one deliberate failure with rollback, one eligibility refusal. All three recorded above.
verification.appliance_state_after: All six services active, maintenance clear, guest portal answering, Activity/Usage/Guest Activity all 200.

what_this_authorises: Nothing beyond itself. PRE-LIVE remains PRE-LIVE, Go-Live is not authorised, telemetry stays off (licensing-only, per the standing decision), and no further controlled migration or privilege change is authorised by this record.
